facts.heading: Anxiety worsening since September
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time, and it has gotten worse since September.
facts.evidence: I'm not really sure where to start. I think I'm just anxious all the time, and it's got worse since September.

facts.heading: Made deputy head at school
facts.content: Hannah was made deputy head at her school. She has taught Year 4 for eleven years.
facts.evidence: I was made deputy head at my school. I've taught Year 4 for eleven years

facts.heading: Fear of being judged
facts.content: Hannah keeps thinking people picked the wrong person for the role. She fears someone will notice she has no idea what she is doing.
facts.evidence: But I keep thinking they picked the wrong person, and that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Anxiety manifests in evenings
facts.content: Hannah's anxiety shows up mostly on Sunday evenings. She rehearses things in her head.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings. My chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Rehearsing potential criticism
facts.content: Hannah rehearses every possible question and what she would say. She imagines how others will think of her if she gets it wrong.
facts.evidence: Every possible question someone might ask, and what I'd say. Then what they'd think of me if I got it wrong.

facts.heading: Fear of being out of depth
facts.content: Hannah imagines people thinking she is out of her depth. She imagines they gave the job to a teacher who cannot lead.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth. That they gave the job to a nice Year 4 teacher who can't actually lead.

facts.heading: Rewrote email four times
facts.content: Hannah rewrote an email to the governors four times last week. The email was about a change to the behaviour policy.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times. A change to the behaviour policy.

facts.heading: Fear of appearing stupid
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr Hargreaves, the chair of governors, would think she was stupid regarding the email.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr Hargreaves, the chair of governors, would think I was stupid.

facts.heading: Mr Hargreaves' reaction
facts.content: Mr Hargreaves has been kind to Hannah. He told her in September he was delighted.
facts.evidence: He's been nothing but kind. He told me in September he was delighted.

facts.heading: Feeling like a liar
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr Hargreaves about her capabilities.
facts.evidence: That makes it worse somehow, because I feel I'm lying to him.

facts.heading: Pretending to be capable
facts.content: Hannah feels she is pretending to be someone who knows what she is doing.
facts.evidence: About being capable. As if I'm pretending.

facts.heading: Comparing to mother's career
facts.content: Hannah compares her work to her mother's career. She thinks everything she does would have been done better by her mother.
facts.evidence: Everything I do, I think, would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother's influence
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a headteacher for twenty years. People in the village still praise her.
facts.evidence: She was a headteacher for twenty years. Everyone in the village still stops me to say what a wonderful head she was.

facts.heading: Mother's retirement
facts.content: Hannah's mother retired six years ago. A library in the village is named after her.
facts.evidence: She retired six years ago and they've named a library after her.

facts.heading: Mother's feedback
facts.content: Hannah's mother says Hannah has always worried too much and should stop being silly.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Feeling like a fuss
facts.content: When her mother gives this feedback, Hannah feels like she is making a fuss.
facts.evidence: It makes me feel I'm making a fuss.

facts.heading: Waking up at four AM
facts.content: Hannah is awake at four every morning. She goes through a to-do list.
facts.evidence: That I'm awake at four every morning. I fall asleep fine, then I'm awake at four going through the to-do list.

facts.heading: Waking due to work stress
facts.content: Hannah has been waking up at four since the second week of term. She drinks a lot of coffee to cope.
facts.evidence: Since about the second week of term. I drink a lot of coffee to get through the day, which I know doesn't help.

facts.heading: Excessive coffee consumption
facts.content: Hannah drinks five or six cups of coffee daily.
facts.evidence: Five or six.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms during afternoons
facts.content: Hannah experiences a fast heart rate and shaky hands in the afternoons.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky.

facts.heading: Hiding physical symptoms
facts.content: Hannah had to leave a meeting to splash her face with water.
facts.evidence: Last Thursday I had to leave a meeting to splash my face with water.

facts.heading: Partner's advice on feelings
facts.content: Ben suggested Hannah should just enjoy the situation.
facts.evidence: He says I should just enjoy it.

facts.heading: Feeling guilty and alone
facts.content: Hannah feels guilty and a bit alone when Ben offers advice.
facts.evidence: Guilty, and a bit alone.

facts.heading: Partner's profession and view
facts.content: Ben is an engineer and thinks problems can be fixed.
facts.evidence: He's an engineer, he thinks if something's a problem you fix it.

facts.heading: Difficulty with social connections
facts.content: Hannah has lost friends at school due to her new role.
facts.evidence: Not any more, not really. I used to eat lunch in the Year 4 corridor with the others. Now I'm their line manager and it's awkward.

facts.heading: Missing former school environment
facts.content: Hannah misses her class and the children.
facts.evidence: I miss them. I miss my class too.

facts.heading: Missing children's experiences
facts.content: Hannah misses the daily experience of children getting something new.
facts.evidence: The children, honestly. The daily bit where a child gets something for the first time.

facts.heading: Desire for promotion
facts.content: Hannah thought she wanted the promotion and said yes because she couldn't say no.
facts.evidence: I thought I did. I said yes in the room because I couldn't say no to her.

facts.heading: Tears about the promotion
facts.content: Hannah cried after saying yes to the promotion.
facts.evidence: Then I went home and cried.

facts.heading: Tears about fear of returning
facts.content: Hannah's tears were about fear and never getting back.
facts.evidence: Fear, I think. And that I'd never get to go back.

facts.heading: Last time feeling relaxed
facts.content: Hannah felt properly relaxed during the summer holidays.
facts.evidence: The summer holidays. We went walking in the Lakes, and I didn't think about school once for ten days.

facts.heading: Relaxation during holiday
facts.content: During the holiday, nobody expected anything of Hannah.
facts.evidence: Nobody expected anything of me. I was just walking.

facts.heading: Pre-term stress return
facts.content: Hannah was a wreck the week before term started.
facts.evidence: The week before term I was a wreck again.

facts.heading: Inability to eat on Sunday
facts.content: Hannah could not eat on Sunday before term started.
facts.evidence: I couldn't eat on the Sunday.

facts.heading: Tried writing down good things
facts.content: Hannah started writing down what went well each evening. This helped for about two weeks.
facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening. Small things. A child laughing, a good email. It helped for about two weeks

facts.heading: Stopped writing due to feeling silly
facts.content: Hannah stopped writing because she felt silly about it.
facts.evidence: and then I stopped, because I felt silly. As if I were bragging to myself in a notebook. Noticing what went well is not the same as bragging. It just felt that way.

facts.heading: Wants to avoid feeling like fraud
facts.content: Hannah wants to do her job without feeling like a fraud.
facts.evidence: I'd like to do the job without feeling like a fraud.

facts.heading: Goal for Tuesday at work
facts.content: Hannah wants to walk into a meeting without rehearsing it first and send only one email.
facts.evidence: Walking into a meeting and not rehearsing it first. Sending an email once.

facts.heading: Goal for Sunday evening
facts.content: Hannah wants to be able to sit on the sofa in the evening without stomach knots.
facts.evidence: Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.

facts.heading: Feeling lighter after sharing
facts.content: Hannah felt lighter and a bit tearful after stating her goals out loud.
facts.evidence: Lighter. A bit tearful, actually.

facts.heading: Has not told Ben about issue
facts.content: Hannah has not told anyone how bad things are. Ben does not know about the four a.m. issue.
facts.evidence: That it's the first time I've told anyone how bad it is. Not even Ben knows about the four a.m.

facts.heading: Fear of telling Ben
facts.content: Hannah feels scared about telling Ben how bad things are. She thinks he would probably be hurt.
facts.evidence: Scary. He'd probably be hurt that I didn't say sooner.

facts.heading: Plan to tell Ben this week
facts.content: Hannah might try telling Ben this week.
facts.evidence: I might try this week.

facts.heading: Helpful time to tell Ben
facts.content: Hannah thinks a quiet moment on a Saturday morning over breakfast would help her tell Ben.
facts.evidence: If I choose a quiet moment. Not on a Sunday evening, then I'm too wound up. Saturday morning, perhaps? Yes, over breakfast. He's always in a good mood then.

facts.heading: Will try evening notebook again
facts.content: Hannah agreed to try the evening notebook again for a week.
facts.evidence: I could. I'll put it by the kettle so I don't forget.

facts.heading: Nearly cancelled session this morning
facts.content: Hannah nearly cancelled the session this morning.
facts.evidence: Only that I nearly cancelled this morning. I'm glad I didn't.
